job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Engagement: Variable hours available

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Netball

Reporting to: Netball Pathway Lead

About the Role:

To deliver high-quality coaching sessions, planning training programmes, and supporting administrative tasks to ensure the smooth running and development of each squad, working across a range of age groups and performance levels within the Netball Pathway.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Support with the implementation of the vision and culture of the Nottingham Forest Netball Pathway.

  • To work with the various coaches across the pathway in creating high performance environments enabling each athlete to develop their technical, tactical, physical and psychological competences.

  • To work closely with the Pathway Head Coach & Sport Science Sports Medicine team to support delivery of a high quality periodised training and competition programmes for targeted players.

  • Committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of young people

What are we looking for:

  • UKCC Level 2 (E) and above

  • Experience of coaching netball within a performance environment

  • Experience of working with athletes aged between 14-19 within a performance environment

  • Excellent athlete management experience

  • Experience of planning & implementing a high-performance program

  • An ability to inspire individuals, build trust and a create a positive & ambitious team culture

  • An ability to balance Nottingham Forest Netball responsibilities with other commitments

  • An ability to work in a team

  • An ability to articulate tactical changes and technical improvements to athletes in a pressurised situation in a concise and meaningful manner

  • Knowledge of HUDL and Performance Analysis

  • An understanding of Roses Development Framework

job.title: Host Family Provider
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Contract: Temporary engagement

Location: Within three miles (15 minutes), easy access to The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Working Arrangements: Remote

Closing Date For Applications: INSERT

About the Role:

We are recruiting for host families who can provide accommodation for our Academy players to support them living away from home. This is a unique and rewarding opportunity to make a real difference to their experience and provide vital support to the players as they develop as young people alongside their football.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Provide a homely and friendly environment for our young people

  • Support with the development of our young people in your care with their independent living and self-care skills

  • Include our young people in family life as much as they feel comfortable with

  • Provide access to a private bedroom, bathroom, laundry facilities, and communal areas of the house

  • Provide a nutritious evening meal 

  • Report any welfare concerns to the Safeguarding and Welfare team should they occur.

  • Allow access from the Club for regular inspection and visits throughout the season.

  • Adhere to any further and ongoing requirements of Host Families, as outlined in the application process, guidance will be provided by the Club on this. 

What are we looking for:

  • Provide a warm, welcoming and safe environment for our young person

  • Provide the young person with their own private bedroom and relevant amenities 

  • Excellent communication and listening skills

  • Ability to cope with the young person's flexible schedule throughout the football season

  • Previous experience of working with young people

  • Ability to promote and demonstrate anti-discriminatory practice 

As part of the recruitment process the Club would need to conduct a number of home visits to determine suitability and ensure the home meets the requirements for hosting young people within the Academy.

Forest For Everyone

We continue to develop policies and practices that promote equality, diversity, inclusion and mental wellbeing across our workforce. To help us measure progress and hold ourselves accountable, we ask all applicants to provide accurate diversity information during the recruitment process.

As part of this commitment, we work hard to ensure our recruitment processes are fair, inclusive, and accessible to everyone. If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme. job.title: Safety Supervisor (Casual)
job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Engagement: Casual position offering variable hours on a flexible basis

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Safety & Security

Reporting to: Safety Officer

About the Role:

In addition to all roles outlined in the Steward Job Description, Supervisors should ensure, as far as is reasonably practicable, they have prepared a safe environment to facilitate the safety of all attendees at events held at the Stadium.

To ensure that those stewards under your supervision feel able to perform their roles, it is essential that you remain visible and accessible, routinely offering support, encouragement, and advice. Ensuring the delivery of excellent customer care is essential to your role.

You will be expected to be involved in managing incidents within your area of responsibility, including dealing with breaches of ground regulations, searching of spectators and performing ejections. You will also be required to assist with queue management within the stadium and in the areas outside.

Supervisors will work within the law and the event regulations as set down by the Club in accordance with the Stadium Safety Certificate.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Attend the Stadium at given dates and times as directed by the Stewarding Services Lead

  • Attend pre-event briefings, noting anything specific to your area as well as ensuring all information is understood and what your areas of responsibility are

  • Brief stewards under your supervision, relaying information relevant to the event as well as reminding them of the threat of terrorism and emergency procedures

job.title: Academy Education Officer
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Department: Academy Education

Reporting to: Head of Education and Audit Coordinator

Closing Date For Applications: 5th August 2026

About the Role:

Nottingham Forest Academy has a clear aim of building on its excellent history and strong back story with the following vision ‘develop a world-class Academy which develops players of Premier League and International Standard. Recognised as a genuine EPPP Category One Academy differentiated by ‘emotion’ and ‘innovation’, this post will be held by an exceptional leader to continue our journey and further develop the excellent young players, people, strategy and methodology we have in place.

The post holder will support the delivery of the Academy Education programme (Scholarship, Full Time Training Model and Hybrid Training Model). The post holder is required to support the academic progression of Academy players aged between under 9 and under 18 to ensure that learners are achieving the highest possible education outcomes in line with the Academy Strategy and exceed the full requirements of the Category 1 Academy determined by the EPPP.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • To work under the direct instruction of the Head of Education and Audit Co-Ordintaor to support the teaching and learning activities of all Academy players.

  • Support with the delivery of the Academy Education Programme (Scholarship, Full Time Training Model and Hybrid Training Model) from an academic and administrative perspective.

  • Planning and delivery of the BTEC Level 3 provision for the Academy.

  • Assess and mark work in line with the BTEC Assessment plan set out by the Premier League.

  • Support the Intervention programme to support learners who are not making expected progress on the BTEC Level 3 programme

  • Be the key point of contact for all education matters on the Full Time Training Model including delivery and coordination of education intervention sessions.

  • Assist with the Co-ordination and delivery of the schoolboy hybrid education programme including liaison with schools of schoolboys in the 12-16 age groups.

  • Liaise with schools to collect academic data every 12 weeks for players on both Part Time Training and Hybrid Training Models to track and monitor academic progress.

  • Build new relationships / partnerships with schools, educational institutions and organisations that will enhance The Academy.

  • Ensure all administration work is completed accurately and within the time scale set by the Head of Academy and /or Head of Education/Assistant Head of Education.

  • Assist in creating a positive and purposeful learning environment for all learners.

  • Assist in creating an inclusive and safe environment for all learners ensuring all have equal access to opportunities to learn and develop.

  • Deal with any safeguarding issues that may arise by reporting them to via Myconcern and to the Academy Safeguarding Manager.

  • Participate in any CPD courses that are deemed relevant to your role

  • Lead on your CPD to ensure you are enhancing your development within the role.

  • Build and maintain effective relationships with governing bodies and external stakeholders to help shape the external environment, maximise student development opportunities, through appropriate challenge and varied experiences.

  • Ensure full adherence to safer recruitment practices and procedures across all Academy staff recruitment activities.

  • Be accountable for maintaining and embedding Nottingham Forest’s values, standards, and behaviours across all Academy staff and players at all times.

  • Ensure the effective use of the Football IP platform across the Education department, in line with established processes, expectations, and reporting requirements.

  • Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, as required, demonstrating progress and outcomes against the Academy strategy.

What are we looking for:

  • Postgraduate Certificate in Education (PGCE) and Qualified Teacher Status (QTS) essential for this role.

  • Degree level education or equivalent essential

  • Knowledge and experience of delivery of a Core Subject (Desirable)

  • Experience of Safeguarding/Safeguarding role desirable

  • Demonstrable experience of secondary education teaching along with successful completion of probation period.

  • Experience of working in an elite sporting environment

  • Sound organisational skills, able to prioritise and manage own workload.

Forest For Everyone

We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.

Disability Confident Committed Employer

We are a Disability Confident Committed employer.  We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions.  If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below.  The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check or an enhanced DBS check. The results of a DBS check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act in a proportionate manner when deciding whether or not to proceed with the appointment.

An FA Enhanced DBS disclosure is required for all relevant new appointments to the Club. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions or reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that may have been incurred. job.title: Lead Academy Physical Performance Coach
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Department: Academy Sports Science and Medicine

Reporting to: Head of Academy Performance & Medical

Closing Date For Applications: 25th August 2026

About the Role:

Nottingham Forest Academy has a clear aim of building on its excellent history and strong back story with the following vision ‘develop a world-class Academy which develops players of Premier League and International Standard. Recognised as a genuine EPPP Category One Academy differentiated by ‘emotion’ and ‘innovation’, this post will be held by an exceptional leader to continue our journey and further develop the excellent young players, people, strategy and methodology we have in place.

This post is expected to optimise the availability and athletic development of Academy players through the provision, monitoring and passionate delivery of an evidence based physical development programme, in line with the Nottingham Forest Football Club Academy performance syllabus. As part of an MDT, you will work directly with the professional development phase (PDP) regarding all aspects of Sports Science and Performance on a day-to-day basis, to exceed the requirements of a Category 1 Academy as determined by EPPP.

This role is primarily working with the B Team and the transition of players from the Academy to the Senior team, providing on-field performance support and assisting in the off-field athletic development programme. It will also require working with the Player Pathways Manager to aid in the physical development and monitoring of loan players.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Provide professional and world leading physical performance support for all registered Academy players including individual programmes and long-term athletic development plans.

  • In association with the academy coaches, organise the weekly training plans and long-term programmes for academy age group players with a primary responsibility for the B team. This should include responsibility for players transitioning between the U18s, B-Team and Men's First Team squads for training and matches.

  • Work closely across the Academy and Senior Performance departments in supporting the transitions of Academy players to First Team football.

  • Ensure Sport Science and S&C provision including session plans, gym sessions and testing are uploaded into the appropriate AMS and Football iP within 24 hours.

  • Manage all pitch related physical performance in co-operation with other MDT team members.

  • Ensure testing and monitoring practices are consistently implemented and evaluated to inform practice.

  • Assist in Talent Identification protocols and contribute to the trialling procedures and testing for potential academy players.

  • Manage and lead the development of the PDP performance staff.

  • Educate staff to ensure the maintenance of age specific best practice including the provision of in-service training and appropriate CPD.

  • Collaborate across the Academy Performance department, aligning programming with synonymous athletic development methodologies.

  • Assist where appropriate other members of the performance and medical departments across all NFFC squads and teams, including rehabilitation support.

  • Work with the wider medical team to provide an integrated approach to performance enhancement regarding injury rehabilitation and return to training/play criteria.

  • In conjunction with the medical department, develop age-related prehab and appropriate rehab to minimise injury risk and maximise player availability.

  • Use appropriate databases to monitor and manage player loading, working closely with the multi-disciplinary team to individualise player plans.

  • To contribute to player reviews and audits in order to assess performance and potential.

  • To provide physical performance support at home and away matches across academy squads, primarily the B Team.

  • Lead and support with evidence-based departmental projects.

  • Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, as required, demonstrating progress and outcomes against the Academy strategy.

  • Any other appropriate duties as required by the Academy management team.

  • Responsible for both individual health & safety and that of those who you are responsible for.

  • Ensure the relationship with children and adults at risk is appropriate and language, behaviour and demeanour is suitable. The Company will expect you to undertake training to ensure an understanding of best practice in relation to children and/or adults at risk.

  • You will be responsible for the welfare of children in your care.

What are we looking for:

  • Previous experience working within the support staff of a professional football club.

  • Worked as part of a multi-disciplinary team.

  • Managed and lead a group of performance staff.

  • Delivered applied sports science support to elite individual or team sport athletes.

  • Experience of football programming and periodisation.

  • BASES accreditation or currently undergoing supervised experience.

  • BSc in Sports Science or equivalent.

  • UKSCA or equivalent (or ability to obtain within 6 months).

  • Valid Basic First Aid for Sport Qualification

  • Valid FA Safeguarding Certificate

  • Ability to accurately measure and monitor essential physical components with elite youth athletes using a range of applied technologies.

  • Provide accurate and informative written and verbal reports to a range of key stakeholders.

  • Managing and developing databases to inform the above.

  • Coach youth athletes across a range of fundamental movements.

  • Exhibit age-appropriate communication techniques.

  • Excellent problem solving and decision-making skills

  • Ability to navigate through courageous and challenging conversations.

  • Innovative and creative with the ability to think outside the box.

  • Knowledge of the Elite Player Performance Plan (EPPP) and associated audit process.

  • Ambitious and driven with a hunger to own and develop an exciting project.

  • Excellent knowledge of development processes and modern performance services.

  • Given the nature of role the individual must be able to deal with sensitive information in a very private and confidential way and must be a team member that people can trust.

  • Creative presentation and delivery skills.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills with an adaptability to work with members of staff across departments.

  • Ability to work under pressure and willing to work unsociable hours.

  • Dedicated to self-improvement and personal development in a very creative way.

  • Organised, methodical and logical approach to work but with a creative spark.

  • High level I.T. and presentation skills.

  • Positive and high energy outlook with an ability to influence and motivate.

  • Ability to accurately measure and monitor essential physical components with elite youth athletes using a range of applied technologies.

  • Provide accurate and informative written and verbal reports to a range of key stakeholders.

  • Managing and developing databases to inform the above.

  • Coach youth athletes across a range of fundamental movements and multi-sport activities.

  • Exhibit age-appropriate communication techniques.

  • Excellent problem solving and decision-making skills.

  • Ability to navigate through courageous and challenging conversations.

  • Innovative and creative with the ability to think outside the box.

Desirable:

  • Previous experience delivering Strength & Conditioning with youth athletes.

  • Have used maturational data and knowledge to deliver appropriate physical development and injury reduction strategies in a team sport setting.

  • An understanding of basic sports nutrition for youth athletes.

  • Research and development experience in Strength and Conditioning, injury prevention and rehabilitation.

  • A postgraduate degree in sports science (or another relevant discipline).

  • Football coaching qualifications.

  • Relevant teaching qualification.

  • ISAK Accreditation

  • Knowledge of and ability to coach and integrate football skills and techniques into strength and conditioning sessions where appropriate.

  • Experience in health and safety duties and responsibilities appropriate to the post

  • Flair for building internal and external networks, productive relationships to share information and ideas, improving working practices

Forest For Everyone

We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.

Ensure testing and monitoring practices are consistently implemented and evaluated to inform practice. - Assist in Talent Identification protocols and contribute to the trialling procedures and testing for potential academy players. - Manage and lead the development of the PDP performance staff. - Educate staff to ensure the maintenance of age specific best practice including the provision of in-service training and appropriate CPD. - Use appropriate databases to monitor and manage player loading, working closely with the multi-disciplinary team to individualise player plans. - To contribute to player reviews and audits in order to assess performance and potential. - To provide physical performance support at home and away matches across academy squads, primarily the B Team. - Lead and support with evidence-based departmental projects. - Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, as required, demonstrating progress and outcomes against the Academy strategy. - Any other appropriate duties as required by the Academy management team. - Responsible for both individual health & safety and that of those who you are responsible for. - Ensure the relationship with children and adults at risk is appropriate and language, behaviour and demeanour is suitable. The Company will expect you to undertake training to ensure an understanding of best practice in relation to children and/or adults at risk. - You will be responsible for the welfare of children in your care.

job.title: Academy Nutritionist
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Department: Academy Sports Science and Medicine

Reporting to: Head of Academy Performance & Medical

Closing Date For Applications: 25th August 2026

About the Role:

Nottingham Forest Academy has a clear aim of building on its excellent history and strong back story with the following vision ‘develop a world-class Academy which develops players of Premier League and International Standard. Recognised as a genuine EPPP Category One Academy differentiated by ‘emotion’ and ‘innovation’, this post will be held by an exceptional leader to continue our journey and further develop the excellent young players, people, strategy and methodology we have in place.

To enhance and deliver our performance nutrition strategy at the Academy, providing high level, evidence based nutritional support that optimises the performance of our Academy players, ensuring an appropriate support and education programme is provided at each phase.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Design and deliver an individual diet and nutrition programme for players that aligns to the requirements of the Academy Strategy and the Elite Player Performance Programme.

  • Develop and deliver player-centered nutrition programmes and provide individualised 1-1 nutrition support to young players in the academy, including loan players.

  • Provide insights based nutritional support for injury and rehabilitation programmes for youth players, in conjunction with the Multi-Disciplinary Team (MDT).

  • Develop and implement innovative and evidence-based nutrition curriculum and education sessions and resources to increase nutrition knowledge throughout the Academy levels for players, parents, host families and colleagues.

  • In conjunction with the MDT, assist with player fitness and strength development, and body composition through nutritional interventions.

  • Measuring and monitoring of players body composition data.

  • Work collaboratively with the MDT on the development of each player as part of the 6-12 weekly multidisciplinary review process.

  • Support match days as directed to assist/implement nutritional provision and provide post game recovery support where appropriate.

  • Maintain records of all nutrition interventions and track measurable outcomes linked to nutritional practices (body composition, nutritional knowledge, anti-doping awareness, hydration etc.). Provide regular reports to the Head of Academy and the Academy Management Team.

  • Working with the MDT and first team practitioners, create individual plans to bridge the gap from academy performance requirements to senior football performance levels, ensuring loan players are provided nutritional support whilst away from the club.

  • Work collaboratively with kitchen and catering staff to ensure adequate food service and provision aligning with nutritional requirements on training and match days.

  • Complete relevant stock checks for supplements, track consumption in line with anti-doping regulations and provide updates for relevant orders.

  • Provide appropriate support and direction to the Performance Team work placement students.

  • To provide performance support where appropriate at home/away matches.

  • Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, as required, demonstrating progress and outcomes against the Academy strategy.

  • Engage in CPD relevant to sports nutrition and be willing to participate in research if the opportunity arises.

  • Any other appropriate duties as required by the Academy management team.

  • Responsible for both individual health & safety and that of those who you are responsible for.

  • Ensure the relationship with children and adults at risk is appropriate and language, behaviour and demeanour is suitable. The Company will expect you to undertake training to ensure an understanding of best practice in relation to children and/or adults at risk.

  • You will be responsible for the welfare of children in your care.

What are we looking for:

  • MSC in sports nutrition, sports science or a related discipline (or working towards)

  • ISAK level 1

  • Practitioner Registrant on UK Sport & Exercise Nutrition Register (Graduate or Practitioner registration).

  • Previous professional experience in the Sports Science field (Sports Nutrition)

  • Experience in the provision of nutritional support to professional athletes and coaches to support performance.

  • Experience in designing and delivering nutritional education and appropriate resource.

  • Naturally collaborative with a strong set of inter-personal coaching skills.

  • Ability to work flexible hours and travel when required.

  • Worked as part of a multi-disciplinary team.

  • Knowledge of the Elite Player Performance Plan (EPPP) and associated audit process.

  • Ambitious and driven with a hunger to own and develop an exciting project.

  • Excellent knowledge of development processes and modern nutrition services.

  • Given the nature of role the individual must be able to deal with sensitive information in a very private and confidential way and must be a team member that people can trust.

  • Creative presentation and delivery skills.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills with an adaptability to work with members of staff across departments.

  • Ability to work under pressure and willing to work unsociable hours.

  • Dedicated to self-improvement and personal development in a very creative way.

  • Organised, methodical and logical approach to work but with a creative spark.

  • High level I.T. and presentation skills.

  • Positive and high energy outlook with an ability to influence and motivate.

  • Ability to accurately measure and monitor essential physical components with elite youth athletes using a range of applied technologies.

  • Provide accurate and informative written and verbal reports to a range of key stakeholders.

  • Managing and developing databases to inform the above.

  • Excellent problem solving and decision-making skills.

  • Ability to navigate through courageous and challenging conversations.

  • Innovative and creative with the ability to think outside the box.

  • Valid Basic First Aid for Sport Qualification.

  • Valid FA Safeguarding Certificate.

Desirable:

  • Previous experience working within the support staff of a professional sports club.

  • Knowledge of the overall Elite Player Performance Plan (EPPP) and specifically the sports science elements of the EPPP.

  • Experience in health and safety duties and responsibilities appropriate to the post

  • Flair for building internal and external networks, productive relationships to share information and ideas, improving working practices

Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.

Disability Confident Committed Employer

We are a Disability Confident Committed employer.  We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions.  If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below.  The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check or an enhanced DBS check. The results of a DBS check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act in a proportionate manner when deciding whether or not to proceed with the appointment.

An FA Enhanced DBS disclosure is required for all relevant new appointments to the Club. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions or reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that may have been incurred. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed on a DBS disclosure if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements. Failure to satisfy the Club and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment.

This post is expected to optimise the availability and athletic development of Academy players through the provision, monitoring and passionate delivery of an evidence based physical development programme in line with the Nottingham Forest Football Club Academy vision and performance strategy. As part of an MDT, work directly with the U13s to U16s squads regarding all aspects of Sports Science and Performance on a day-to-day basis, exceeding the requirements of a Category 1 Academy as determined by EPPP.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Academy players including individual programmes and long-term athletic development plans in line with the club’s Performance curriculum.

  • Use appropriate databases to monitor and manage player loading, working closely with the multi-disciplinary team to individualise player plans.

  • Manage gym, rehab and pre-activation areas in co-operation with other Performance team members.

  • Monitor player growth and maturation and implement appropriate strategies to aid player development and maximise availability.

  • To liaise with the nutritionist and catering department to ensure all nutritional needs for training and match days are met.

  • To contribute to player reviews and audits to assess performance and potential.

  • To participate in key topics of research to provide clinical based evidence for current and new Performance practices.

  • To provide performance support where appropriate at home/away matches.

  • Work in collaboration with the Professional Development phase to ensure appropriate alignment and transitions for future scholars.

  • Assist where appropriate other members of the Performance and Medical departments across all NFFC squads and teams.

  • In conjunction with the medical department, develop age-related prehab and rehab protocols to minimise injury risk and maximise player availability.

  • Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, as required, demonstrating progress and outcomes against the Academy strategy.

  • Any other appropriate duties as required by the Academy management team.

  • Responsible for both individual health & safety and that of those who you are responsible for.

  • Ensure the relationship with children and adults at risk is appropriate and language, behaviour and demeanour is suitable. The Company will expect you to undertake training to ensure an understanding of best practice in relation to children and/or adults at risk.

What are we looking for:

  • At least two years’ experience in the provision of Performance services to elite athletes.

  • Experience in paediatric physical development.

  • Awareness of maturation monitoring and growth-related injuries, with an understanding of how to apply interventions to manage these.

  • Worked as part of a multi-disciplinary team.

  • Knowledge of the Elite Player Performance Plan (EPPP) and associated audit process.

  • Ambitious and driven with a hunger to own and develop an exciting project.

  • Excellent knowledge of development processes and modern performance services.

  • Given the nature of role the individual must be able to deal with sensitive information in a very private and confidential way and must be a team member that people can trust.

  • Creative presentation and delivery skills.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills with an adaptability to work with members of staff across departments.

  • Ability to work under pressure and willing to work unsociable hours.

  • Dedicated to self-improvement and personal development in a very creative way.

  • Organised, methodical and logical approach to work but with a creative spark.

  • High level I.T. and presentation skills.

  • Positive and high energy outlook with an ability to influence and motivate.

  • Ability to accurately measure and monitor essential physical components with elite youth athletes using a range of applied technologies.

  • Provide accurate and informative written and verbal reports to a range of key stakeholders.

  • Managing and developing databases to inform the above.

  • Coach youth athletes across a range of fundamental movements and multi-sport activities.

  • Exhibit age-appropriate communication techniques.

  • Excellent problem solving and decision-making skills.

  • Ability to navigate through courageous and challenging conversations.

  • Innovative and creative with the ability to think outside the box.

  • BSc in Sports Science or equivalent.

  • UKSCA or equivalent (or ability to obtain within 6 months).

  • CASES accreditation / Currently undergoing supervised experience (or ability to submit application within 6 months)

  • Valid Basic First Aid for Sport Qualification.

  • Valid FA Safeguarding Certificate.

  • Enhanced DBS Check.

  • Safeguarding Children Certificate.

Desirable:

  • Previous experience working within the support staff of a professional sports club.

  • An understanding of basic sports nutrition for youth athletes.

  • Research and development experience in Strength and Conditioning, injury prevention and rehabilitation.

  • A postgraduate degree in sports science (or another relevant discipline).

  • Experience in health and safety duties and responsibilities appropriate to the post

Educate staff to ensure the maintenance of age specific best practice including the provision of in-service training and appropriate CPD. - Provide age-specific performance education seminars to players and parents/guardians at appropriate times during the season to educate on key high-performance topics (e.g. maturation, fitness and dietary matters). - Manage gym, rehab and pre-activation areas in co-operation with other Performance team members. - Monitor player growth and maturation and implement appropriate strategies to aid player development and maximise availability. - To liaise with the nutritionist and catering department to ensure all nutritional needs for training and match days are met. - To contribute to player reviews and audits to assess performance and potential. - To participate in key topics of research to provide clinical based evidence for current and new Performance practices. - To provide performance support where appropriate at home/away matches. - Work in collaboration with the Professional Development phase to ensure appropriate alignment and transitions for future scholars. - Assist where appropriate other members of the Performance and Medical departments across all NFFC squads and teams. - In conjunction with the medical department, develop age-related prehab and rehab protocols to minimise injury risk and maximise player availability. - Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, as required, demonstrating progress and outcomes against the Academy strategy. - Any other appropriate duties as required by the Academy management team. - Responsible for both individual health & safety and that of those who you are responsible for. - Ensure the relationship with children and adults at risk is appropriate and language, behaviour and demeanour is suitable. The Company will expect you to undertake training to ensure an understanding of best practice in relation to children and/or adults at risk. - You will be responsible for the welfare of children in your care.
What are we looking for:
- At least two years’ experience in the provision of Performance services to elite athletes. - Experience in paediatric physical development. - Awareness of maturation monitoring and growth-related injuries, with an understanding of how to apply interventions to manage these. - Worked as part of a multi-disciplinary team. - Knowledge of the Elite Player Performance Plan (EPPP) and associated audit process. - Ambitious and driven with a hunger to own and develop an exciting project. - Excellent knowledge of development processes and modern performance services. - Given the nature of role the individual must be able to deal with sensitive information in a very private and confidential way and must be a team member that people can trust. - Creative presentation and delivery skills. - Excellent interpersonal skills with an adaptability to work with members of staff across departments. - Ability to work under pressure and willing to work unsociable hours. - Dedicated to self-improvement and personal development in a very creative way. - Organised, methodical and logical approach to work but with a creative spark. - High level I.T. and presentation skills. - Positive and high energy outlook with an ability to influence and motivate. - Ability to accurately measure and monitor essential physical components with elite youth athletes using a range of applied technologies. - Provide accurate and informative written and verbal reports to a range of key stakeholders. - Managing and developing databases to inform the above. - Coach youth athletes across a range of fundamental movements and multi-sport activities. - Exhibit age-appropriate communication techniques. - Excellent problem solving and decision-making skills. - Ability to navigate through courageous and challenging conversations. - Innovative and creative with the ability to think outside the box. - BSc in Sports Science or equivalent. - UKSCA or equivalent (or ability to obtain within 6 months). - CASES accreditation / Currently undergoing supervised experience (or ability to submit application within 6 months) - Valid Basic First Aid for Sport Qualification. - Valid FA Safeguarding Certificate. - Enhanced DBS Check. - Safeguarding Children Certificate.
Desirable:
- Previous experience working within the support staff of a professional sports club. - An understanding of basic sports nutrition for youth athletes. - Research and development experience in Strength and Conditioning, injury prevention and rehabilitation. - A postgraduate degree in sports science (or another relevant discipline). - Football coaching qualifications - Experience in health and safety duties and responsibilities appropriate to the post - Flair for building internal and external networks, productive relationships to share information and ideas, improving working practices

job.title: Head of Football Intelligence
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Reporting to: Chief Football Officer

Closing Date For Applications: 25th August 2026

About the Role:

We are looking for an experienced and forward-thinking Head of Football Intelligence to lead the club’s Football Intelligence provision across the First Team, Academy and Women’s programme.

Reporting into the football leadership team, the successful candidate will be responsible for the continuous development of the club’s data and insights strategy, ensuring these are integrated into decision-making processes. This role will combine a mix of strategic leadership and hands-on delivery, supporting performance analysis, recruitment, squad planning and other key football projects.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

People

  • Lead, develop and mentor the Football Intelligence team, helping to create a collaborative and forward-thinking culture.

  • Build and manage strong relationships across the football operation, including recruitment, performance analysis, medical and sports sciences, and football leadership.

  • Communicate complex data insights to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Support the continuous development of the First Team, Academy and Women’s programme.

Product

  • Lead the development of key projects including recruitment models, player and squad profiling, recruitment lists, pre- and post-match analysis, benchmarking frameworks, reporting and other decision-support tools.

  • Deliver data-informed insights and key recommendations to the football leadership team, actively supporting recruitment, squad planning and decision-making.

  • Oversee and manage the club’s football data ecosystem, ensuring that all pipelines, reports, infrastructure and tools support the club’s long-term strategy and goals.

Process

  • Working in close collaboration with the senior football leadership team, define and implement a long-term Football Intelligence strategy and vision.

  • Work with and across all football departments to integrate data-informed insights into existing workflows and decision-making processes.

  • Where required, manage data budgets, contracts and relationships with external data providers, ensuring scalable and sustainable insights delivery.

What are we looking for:

Essential

  • Relevant qualification in Data Science, Sports Science, Performance Analysis or equivalent.

  • Significant experience working within elite football in a football analytics role.

  • Proven experience translating complex football data into clear, actionable insights for technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Strong understanding of recruitment, match analysis and key decision-making processes.

  • Experience developing decision-support tools including player profiling and reporting.

  • Strong working knowledge of SQL, Python and/or R.

  • Experience working with data visualisation platforms and web apps.

  • Experience leading projects and collaborating across multidisciplinary football departments.

  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management and presentation skills.

  • Strong understanding of technical and tactical aspects of football.

Desirable

  • Previous experience leading or mentoring a data insights team at elite level.

  • Experience managing the development of football data infrastructure and ETL pipelines.

  • Experience working with event, tracking and physical performance datasets.

  • Experience working with football data providers and other external solutions.

  • Evidence of continued professional development through relevant certifications, research or industry engagement.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.

Disability Confident Committed Employer

We are a Disability Confident Committed employer.  We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions.  If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below.  The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check or an enhanced DBS check. The results of a DBS check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act in a proportionate manner when deciding whether or not to proceed with the appointment.

An FA Enhanced DBS disclosure is required for all relevant new appointments to the Club. job.title: Education Assistant (Casual)
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Engagement: Casual position offering variable hours on a flexible basis

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Department: Academy Education

Reporting to: Head of Education & Audit Co-ordinator

Closing Date For Applications: 25th August 2026

About the Role:

Nottingham Forest Academy has a clear aim of building on its excellent history and strong back story with the following vision ‘develop a world-class Academy which develops players of Premier League and International Standard. Recognised as a genuine EPPP Category One Academy differentiated by ‘emotion’ and ‘innovation’, this post will be held by an exceptional leader to continue our journey and further develop the excellent young players, people, strategy and methodology we have in place.

The post holder will support the delivery of the Academy Education programme (Scholarship, Full Time Training Model and Hybrid Training Model). The post holder is required to support the academic progression of Academy players aged between under 9 and under 18 to ensure that learners are achieving the highest possible education outcomes in line with the Academy Strategy and exceed the full requirements of the Category 1 Academy determined by the EPPP.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • To work under the direct instruction of the Head of Education and Audit Co-Ordintaor to support the teaching and learning activities of all Academy players.

  • Support with the delivery of the Academy Education Programme (Scholarship, Full Time Training Model and Hybrid Training Model) from an academic and administrative perspective.

  • Planning and delivery of the BTEC Level 3 provision for the Academy.

  • Assess and mark work in line with the BTEC Assessment plan set out by the Premier League.

  • Support the Intervention programme to support learners who are not making expected progress on the BTEC Level 3 programme

  • Be the key point of contact for all education matters on the Full Time Training Model including delivery and coordination of education intervention sessions.

  • Assist with the Co-ordination and delivery of the schoolboy hybrid education programme including liaison with schools of schoolboys in the 12-16 age groups.

  • Liaise with schools to collect academic data every 12 weeks for players on both Part Time Training and Hybrid Training Models to track and monitor academic progress.

  • Build new relationships / partnerships with schools, educational institutions and organisations that will enhance The Academy.

  • Ensure all administration work is completed accurately and within the time scale set by the Head of Academy and /or Head of Education/Assistant Head of Education.

  • Assist in creating a positive and purposeful learning environment for all learners.

  • Assist in creating an inclusive and safe environment for all learners ensuring all have equal access to opportunities to learn and develop.

  • Deal with any safeguarding issues that may arise by reporting them to via Myconcern and to the Academy Safeguarding Manager.

  • Participate in any CPD courses that are deemed relevant to your role

  • Lead on your CPD to ensure you are enhancing your development within the role.

  • Build and maintain effective relationships with governing bodies and external stakeholders to help shape the external environment, maximise student development opportunities, through appropriate challenge and varied experiences.

  • Ensure full adherence to safer recruitment practices and procedures across all Academy staff recruitment activities.

  • Be accountable for maintaining and embedding Nottingham Forest’s values, standards, and behaviours across all Academy staff and players at all times.

  • Ensure the effective use of the Football IP platform across the Education department, in line with established processes, expectations, and reporting requirements.

  • Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, as required, demonstrating progress and outcomes against the Academy strategy.

What are we looking for:

  • Postgraduate Certificate in Education (PGCE) and Qualified Teacher Status (QTS) essential for this role.

  • Degree level education or equivalent essential

  • Knowledge and experience of delivery of a Core Subject (Desirable)

  • Experience of Safeguarding/Safeguarding role desirable

  • Demonstrable experience of secondary education teaching along with successful completion of probation period.

  • Experience of working in an elite sporting environment

  • Sound organisational skills, able to prioritise and manage own workload.

job.title: First Team Recruitment Analyst
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Reporting to: Recruitment Analyst

Closing Date For Applications: 28th August 2026

About the Role:

Nottingham Forest FC are seeking a Recruitment Analyst to join the scouting department, supporting the full player identification, analysis and reporting process. Reporting to the Lead Recruitment Analyst, the successful candidate will take ownership of a specific positional group across both Senior and Emerging Talent pathways, contributing directly to transfer window strategy and the department's day-to-day operations. The role also carries responsibility for the technical production of player presentations, including video content and dossier compilation.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Lead scouting coverage for assigned positional groups, filtering and prioritising targets.

  • Research, track and evaluate prospective transfer targets throughout the window.

  • Compile detailed player dossiers, written reports and supporting video content to inform recruitment decisions.

  • Attend domestic and international fixtures as part of ongoing live scouting work.

  • Build and maintain a network of contacts within the football industry.

  • Maintain scenario-specific shortlists, kept regularly updated and ready to deliver at any point to support recruitment decisions.

  • Contribute to department operations, including platform management and internal reporting processes.

  • Work collaboratively and adaptably within the wider scouting team, while demonstrating the independence and confidence to take initiative and communicate findings clearly to key stakeholders.

What are we looking for:

Essential:

  • Minimum 3 years' experience working within a competitive first-team recruitment environment.

  • Demonstrable track record in player analysis, with strong position-specific tactical understanding.

  • Proven ability to produce clear, well-structured reports and dossiers.

  • Working knowledge of industry-leading platforms such as Wyscout, SkillCorner and StatsBomb.

  • Strong research capability across market trends and positional requirements.

  • Ability to manage a demanding workload and maintain performance under pressure.

  • Proficient in written and verbal English communication.

  • Proficient in Hudl Studio or comparable video editing software, including the creation of clip libraries and playlists for the players under assessment.

Desirable:

  • Postgraduate qualification in a relevant discipline (e.g. sports science, data analysis, performance analysis).

  • Existing network of contacts within the scouting or recruitment community

job.title: Deputy Safety Officer
job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 37.5 hours a week

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Safety and Security

Reporting to: Head of Safety and Security

Closing Date For Applications: 26th August 2026

About the Role:

The role will be responsible for ensuring, as reasonably practicable, the security of all Club premises, and the safety of all people attending events at The City Ground in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Safety Certificate and the Club’s Policy for Spectator Safety, through the establishment, operations and monitoring of suitable systems and controls, maintaining compliance with all relevant legislation and best practice.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Assisting with co-ordinating and monitoring all matchday safety matters affecting the stadium.

  • Establishing, maintaining and reviewing Safety Policy in line with changes in legislation, best practice and identified problems through appropriate risk assessment.

  • Ensuring that the provisions of the Safety Certificate issues by Nottingham County Council are acted upon.

  • Maintaining compliance with all requirements of the ‘Safety at Sports Grounds’ legislation (The Green Guide) and other advisory documents issued by the Sports Ground Safety Authority.

  • Consulting regularly with senior representatives of Nottinghamshire Police, Fire and Rescue Service, East Midlands Ambulance Service and Nottinghamshire County Council regarding spectator safety and security.

  • Attending Nottinghamshire CC Safety Advisory Group meetings representing Club interests.

  • Liaising with the Emergency Services in the event of critical incidents and keep senior Club officials fully informed of developments.

  • Overseeing and reviewing Stewarding requirements for Matchdays to ensure numbers of staff and allocation complies with the Safety Certificate.

  • Assisting with reviewing and implementing appropriate elements of Health & Safety Legislation in relation to crowd safety and large events, liaising with the Health & Safety Executive and other relevant bodies.

  • Assist with investigating and responding to customer complaints arising from safety & security activities.

  • Liaising with Supporters Associations & assist in the planning of future events.

  • Continually reviewing the operation of the dept and implement actions to improve its effectiveness and keep up to date with changes/trends in football and adopt best practice where appropriate.

  • Liaising with and assist other departments with the preparation and launching of new initiatives.

  • You will be required to work on all home match days and to work across all Club sites including the Stadium, Club offices and Training Ground.

What are we looking for:

  • Experience in similar role involving spectator safety and large crowds at big sporting events.

  • NVQ Level 4 qualification in Spectator Safety or equivalent, or Safety Management qualification or working towards qualification.

  • Highly developed problem-solving skills, is resilient, works well in pressurised and stressful situations.

  • Flexibility to deal with issues out of hours and at short notice.

  • Develop a culture of continuous improvement and the ability to embed this ethos within your team.

  • Fosters a team approach both within and between departments assisting others where appropriate.

  • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate confidently with the public, contractors, employees at all levels in and outside the Club.

  • Strong leadership and management skills, commercial awareness and excellent decision-making skills.

  • Sound organisational skills, able to prioritise and manage own workload and that of allocated staff.

  • The ability to interpret and implement policies as required.

  • Be able to communicate key issues to a wide audience, listen to suggestions, ask probing questions to ensure full understanding of messages.

  • The ability to develop relationships with people quickly, work to build longer term individual, team and department relationships, creating trust and credibility.

  • Have a sound understanding of the financial and relationship management of your own area.

  • Ensure that internal and external satisfaction is a high priority.

  • The ability to complete all necessary tasks required by you and the team, ensuring high standards are always achieved.

  • Be able to persuade others through a well-structured and well-reasoned case.

Forest For Everyone

We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.

Disability Confident Committed Employer

We are a Disability Confident Committed employer.  We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions.  If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below.  The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check or an enhanced DBS check. The results of a DBS check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act in a proportionate manner when deciding whether or not to proceed with the appointment.

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Reporting to: Head of Women and Girls Football

Closing Date For Applications:26th August 2026

About the Role:

The role will involve working as an integral part of the Girls Academy, facilitating the delivery of the performance analysis programme predominantly for the women first team.

The role will require a hard-working individual, who is able to work with a high level of detail and accuracy, whilst being comfortable with operating in a fast-paced, modern environment.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Lead the analysis programme for the Women's First Team.

  • Work closely with the women first team Head Coach and technical team on shaping, facilitating & delivering the analysis programme.

  • Ensure that games & training are covered effectively.

  • Work as part of a collaborative MDT team.

  • Build relationships with wider MDT staff throughout the academy.

  • Undertake self-development to ensure knowledge in all aspects of your role is up to date & industry leading.

  • Filming of women first team training.

  • Travel to home & away to women first team fixtures to film.

  • Help facilitate the filming of Goalkeeper training.

  • Create & help deliver analysis sessions.

  • Support the creation and implementation of Individual Development Plans.

  • Create a team-orientated stats report for women first team.

  • Help generate individualised metrics from match play for players within the women first team.

  • Build and maintain a library of best practice from games and training.

What are we looking for:

  • Previous experience at working at First Team level in an elite sporting environment.

  • Detailed technical and tactical knowledge of football.

  • Postgraduate degree in performance analysis or relevant field.

  • Highly proficient in using Hudl Sportscode & Hudl Studio.

  • Accustomed to leading and delivering analysis sessions to players & staff.

  • Experience filming training and matches with a variety of different equipment.

  • Football Coaching Qualifications (UEFA C License or higher).

  • Experience using SBG Matchtracker (desirable).

- Lead the analysis programme for the Women's First Team. - Work closely with the women first team Head Coach and technical team on shaping, facilitating & delivering the analysis programme. - Ensure that games & training are covered effectively. - Work as part of a collaborative MDT team. - Build relationships with wider MDT staff throughout the academy. - Undertake self-development to ensure knowledge in all aspects of your role is up to date & industry leading. - Filming of women first team training. - Travel to home & away to women first team fixtures to film. - Help facilitate the filming of Goalkeeper training. - Create & help deliver analysis sessions. - Support the creation and implementation of Individual Development Plans. - Create a team-orientated stats report for women first team. - Help generate individualised metrics from match play for players within the women first team. - Build and maintain a library of best practice from games and training.
What are we looking for:
- Previous experience at working at First Team level in an elite sporting environment. - Detailed technical and tactical knowledge of football. - Postgraduate degree in performance analysis or relevant field. - Highly proficient in using Hudl Sportscode & Hudl Studio. - Accustomed to leading and delivering analysis sessions to players & staff. - Experience filming training and matches with a variety of different equipment. - Football Coaching Qualifications (UEFA C License or higher). - Previous experience leading an analysis programme (desirable). - Experience using SBG Matchtracker (desirable). - Experience using Piero (desirable). - Accustomed using Tableau, and handling data, to produce team & individual orientated reports (desirable). - Experience undertaking longitudinal research projects (desirable). - Full UK Driving License (desirable).
Forest For Everyone
We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.
Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.
Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.
Disability Confident Committed Employer
We are a Disability Confident Committed employer. We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions. If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.
If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to theEquality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via theDisability Confident Scheme- please indicate this in your application form below. The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.
Our Commitment to Safeguarding
As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check or an enhanced DBS check. The results of a DBS check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act in a proportionate manner when deciding whether or not to proceed with the appointment.
An FA Enhanced DBS disclosure is required for all relevant new appointments to the Club. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions or reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that may have been incurred. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed on a DBS disclosure if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements. Failure to satisfy the Club and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment.

job.title: Foundation Phase Academy Coach
job.html_description:
JOB TITLE:  Foundation Phase Academy Coach
REPORTING TO:  Academy Technical Director
DEPARTMENT: Sporting
LOCATION:   St. Johns University; Queens & City Football Academy :Orangeburg, New York 
 
POSITION OVERVIEW:
As an Academy Coach you will have the overall responsibility in the continued development of a specific age group. You will be responsible for the delivery of the NYCFC coaching philosophy and managing Individual Development Plans for the players. You will lead the interdisciplinary team in achieving individual and team goals. It is important that you are willing and able to work together across departments and other age groups. You will be responsible for the development program of the team and individuals, working in a multidisciplinary environment. This role will be based in the Foundation Phase. 
 
WHAT YOU’LL DO:
  • Create a learning environment that balances challenges and support for each individual player.
  • Maximize the potential of every player through the delivery of the NYCFC game model and methodology.
  • Deliver the content of all daily training sessions and match preparation, together with your staff.
  • Work cooperatively with other Academy teams and staff and maintain relationships with appropriate internal and external stakeholders.
  • Plan, deliver, and review coaching practices according to the NYCFC methodology, with an action-oriented attitude and a commitment to continual improvement.
  • Work from a periodization model and conduct practice designs to enhance the learning and understanding of NYCFC's game model.
  • Work with other Academy coaches to deliver one-to-one player development support through progressive Individual Development Plans, providing ongoing, specific, and actionable feedback.
  • Understand and adhere to all Competition Guidelines in all entered competitions.
  • Represent NYCFC in a positive manner while carrying out all required responsibilities.
  • Support the continued development and matriculation of Academy players to progress through our system.
  • Engage with, and ensure timely input into, all Academy platforms and software (Smartabase, Taka, etc.).

WHAT YOU’LL BRING:
  • 5+ experience coaching youth academy level.
  • USSF ‘B or A’ license – minimum (required) 
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work multidisciplinary in the context of Soccer. 
  • Valid driver’s license 
  • Knowledge of Microsoft office; PowerPoint, Word, and Excel
  • Knowledge of tactical periodization and how to implement it.
  • A growth mindset and willingness to join the team with enthusiasm and curiosity. 
 
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
  • Applicant must be able to comply with MLS Next Safety and Well-Being policy and any other applicable child safety policies provided to applicants by NYCFC
  • Must be able to work games scheduled which may be at night and on weekends and holidays

COMPENSATION:
This exempt position has an estimated annual base salary range of $62,500-65,000. Final compensation offer amounts are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to demonstrated skill set, years and depth of relevant experience, and some role-dependent factors such as certifications and software expertise. We welcome direct conversations with each candidate about compensation in all of our initial calls.
 
WHAT WE OFFER:
  • Excellent health, dental & vision insurance, with options to fit you and your family’s needs
  • Comprehensive and competitive benefit programs, including maternal & paternal leave
  • Ancillary benefits: Commuter, gym membership, and Citi Bike discounts
  • Your health is important! Our wellness strategy focuses on mental and physical wellbeing through in-office and virtual programs
  • Four complementary tickets to every NYCFC home match
  • Team outings, happy hours, and annual staff gatherings to celebrate our co-workers
  • A dynamic, ambitious, and fun work environment

WHO YOU ARE: 
At New York FC, we are committed to upholding our core club values and our values guide how we show up and work together every day.  If you share our values listed below, please consider NYCFC as a great place for you to work (and play):
 
Acts Honorably: listens and communicates respectfully, without judgement
Engages Collaboratively: provides and seeks constructive feedback to and from peers, proactively sharing appreciation for quality contributions of others
Champions Inclusion: celebrates the value of differences recognizing the value in the unique backgrounds and lived experiences of every team member
Drives Forward: embraces new opportunities with curiosity and a focus on improvement and innovation
Shows Heart: demonstrates passion for the Club and sport, operating as an NYCFC ambassador in encouraging and inspiring that passion in others
 
NEW YORK CITY FOOTBALL CLUB OVERVIEW:
At New York City FC, we are on a mission to build this city into one of the soccer capitals of the world. The Club was announced as Major League Soccer’s 20th franchise and is the first and only MLS team located within the five boroughs of New York City. The Club has qualified for the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs nine times over the past 10 seasons, winning MLS Cup in 2021. Games are available to stream via an Apple TV subscription, providing every match of the MLS regular season, the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, annual Leagues Cup tournament, the MLS All-Star Game, the Campeones Cup, and more all in one place and with no blackouts. New York City FC is building New York City’s first-ever soccer-specific stadium, Etihad Park, which is set to open in 2027. For more information, please visit: www.newyorkcityfc.com.

New York City FC is also one of 12 clubs comprising City Football Group and counts Manchester City FC, Melbourne City FC, Yokohama F-Marinos, Girona FC, Montevideo City Torque, Shenzhen Peng City FC, Lommel SK, ESTAC Troyes, Palermo FC, Bahia, and Club Bolívar among its sister clubs.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.  This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
