Description
U.S. Soccer Overview
The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.
We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.
U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.
Position Description
The Safeguarding Manager, Youth Engagement is U.S. Soccer's subject-matter expert on safeguarding for youth participants of the game. For the purposes of this role, "youth participants" means all under-18 participants, including minor players, minor referees, and other young people who take part in soccer activities, programs, and events. The role leads safeguarding prevention and education across the youth game and provides youth participant expertise across the wider safeguarding team.
At its core, this role is about culture and the young people at the heart of the game. Meeting regulatory requirements is essential, but not the finish line. Success is measured by whether young people feel safe, heard, and genuinely valued in soccer, and whether the adults around them build environments where that is the norm. Youth voice and youth agency are not add-ons to this work; they are its purpose.
This is a standards-and-enablement role. Rather than personally delivering every program, the Manager sets the frameworks, builds the tools and learning, and equips U.S. Soccer staff, Member Organizations, and partners to create and sustain safe, healthy environments themselves. Given a period of significant growth and major events, priorities will be delivered in phases, sequenced with the Vice President of Safeguarding: foundational standards and education first, then deeper assurance and member capability over time.
To succeed, the Manager brings deep expertise in safeguarding and child protection, a strong command of the regulatory landscape governing minor athletes within the Olympic and Paralympic Movement, and a proven ability to translate standards into practical policy, education, and culture across grassroots, community, and elite settings. Above all, the Manager is committed to working directly with youth athletes, championing their voice, agency, and wellbeing at every stage of their participation.
The role contributes across U.S. Soccer's safeguarding methodology of prevention, reporting, and response. The Manager designs and embeds the policies, learning, and pathways that prevent harm before it occurs. Working closely with the Reporting and Resolution team, the Manager also helps build clear, trusted reporting systems, ensuring concerns can be raised easily, disclosures are acted on appropriately, and learning flows back into prevention. The Manager supports this function as an expert but does not perform case management; intake, investigation, and adjudication sit with the Reporting and Resolution team and the U.S. Center for SafeSport, in line with federal law and U.S. Soccer policy.
The role reports to the Vice President of Safeguarding - Prevention & Education, and works closely with the National Team Safeguarding Manager, providing minor-participant expertise wherever minors or participants at heightened risk are involved (including the youth and disability National Teams). It also partners with the Director of Safeguarding Operations, the Reporting and Resolution team, and other programming members, such as Recreation and Soccer Forward.
Primary Responsibilities
Subject-Matter Expertise & Sector Leadership
- Serve as Subject-Matter Expert: Act as a key internal expert on youth athletes and youth participant safeguarding spanning regulation, recognized best practice, and the evidence base for U.S. Soccer. Maintain current expertise in applicable requirements (the U.S. Center for SafeSport Minor Athlete Abuse Prevention Policies (MAAPP), the SafeSport Code, USOPC requirements including evolving background-check and training standards, and applicable state mandatory-reporting law) alongside leading safeguarding frameworks and research, including evidence-based, trauma-informed, and child-centered prevention practice. With the wider Safeguarding team, support the translation of regulatory change and emerging evidence into clear, actionable internal guidance, and contribute to external guidance for Members and partners. - Serve as an Advisor: Provide expert advice and support to the wider Safeguarding Team and U.S. Soccer operations wherever youth or participants at heightened risk are involved, including the youth national teams, the disability National Teams, age-group camps, talent-identification events, and the transition of minor participants into the senior environment. - Contribute Thought Leadership: Stay at the leading edge of youth safeguarding in soccer, building relationships with U.S. Soccer Members, peer NGBs, and child-protection experts, and researching and briefing the organization on emerging best practices and risks to minor participants. Maintain particular focus on the digital environment, including online grooming, harmful contact through social and gaming platforms, sextortion, image-based abuse, and AI-enabled threats, translating insight into refreshed prevention controls and helping to champion a positive, child-centered safeguarding culture.
Policies, Standards & Safe Environments
- Develop Policies and Standards:Support the development and maintenance of safeguarding policies, codes of conduct, and operating standards that apply to youth participants, including recreation, community, commercial, and event settings, with practical implementation tools that make them usable for youth, staff, volunteers, contractors, and partners. - Advance Inclusive and Accessible Safeguarding: Ensure safeguarding standards, learning, and reporting routes are inclusive and accessible through addressing the elevated and specific risks faced by disabled participants and other groups at heightened risk across the youth and grassroots game, including disability soccer programs, and equipping programs to make safe participation genuinely accessible to all. - Enable Safe Engagement in Youth Activities: Set and advise on safeguarding standards for any activity that involves or depicts youth participants, including photo and video shoots, public appearances, ambassador and talent engagements, and the use of minors' image and likeness in marketing, merchandise, and collectibles. Define consent, chaperoning, and supervision requirements in partnership with Marketing, Commercial, and Legal, keeping young people's dignity and agency at the center of how they are represented. - Enable Safe Facilities, Events, and Activations: Provide the safeguarding standards, planning, and risk-assessment support that keep minors safe at U.S. Soccer venues, events, and activations whenever they are present or their interests are engaged, including the national training center, visiting youth groups, camps, clinics, tours, and event-day supervision, trusted-adult, and reporting arrangements. Support U.S. Soccer Members in building the same safe practices for their own youth participants.
Education, Training & Capacity Building
- Build Learning and Education Assets:Lead the development of safeguarding learning content with and for youth participants and the adults who engage with them, using blended digital, virtual, and in-person delivery designed to be age-appropriate, accessible, and effective across a diverse, multilingual community. - Build Member Capacity: Strengthen the safeguarding capacity and capability of Member Organizations through toolkits, train-the-trainer models, and ongoing support, scaling consistent standards across a membership of millions. This includes supporting the Safe Soccer Clearance program from a youth participant perspective, so that the training, screening, and clearance of those working with minors remain appropriate and effective.
Program Safeguarding: Recreation & Community
- Support Recreation and Schools Programming:Act as a safeguarding partner to Soccer in Schools and recreation initiatives, ensuring program models, screening, supervision standards, and reporting pathways are appropriate for school and community delivery. - Embed Safeguarding in Community Engagement: Build safeguarding into Soccer Forward and community and social-impact programming through a child-centered, inclusive, “safeguarding-by-design” approach.
Collaboration, Monitoring & Continuous Improvement
- Make Reporting and Response Accessible to Minors and Communities:Work with the Reporting and Resolution team to ensure reporting and response systems are appropriate, accessible, and trusted for youth participants and the communities they come from. Routes for raising concerns should be age-appropriate, low-barrier, culturally and linguistically accessible, and well understood by young people, families, and grassroots organizations, with disclosures recognized and escalated appropriately. - Collaborate Across the Organization:Partner across the Reporting and Resolution team, Legal, Coaching Education, Commercial, Facilities, and Membership to align policy, education, and delivery, and feed learning back into prevention.
Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Child Protection, Social Work, Education, Public Health, Sport Management, Criminal Justice, or a related field (or equivalent experience) - Safeguarding Expertise & Experience:Minimum of 5 years in safeguarding, child protection, or minor welfare, including hands-on experience designing and implementing prevention measures and delivering policy and education programs at scale, experience with safeguarding in a sporting environment and a strong working knowledge of the U.S. child-protection landscape (U.S. Center for SafeSport and MAAPP requirements; state mandatory-reporting obligations), with a demonstrated track record of building child-centered, youth-voice-led safeguarding culture, not only implementing policy and meeting compliance requirements - Learning Design:Demonstrated experience designing and delivering effective learning and training frameworks (digital, blended, and in-person) for varied audiences including young people, and leveraging digital learning ecosystems (LMS, content delivery, learning analytics), with awareness of online-safety and digital-risk trends affecting young people - Leadership & Project Management:Proven ability to lead projects, influence across functions without direct authority, and contribute to strategic decision-making; capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments - Judgment & Discretion: Excellent judgment, the ability to recognize risk and the limits of the role and escalate appropriately, and the highest standards of integrity and confidentiality when handling sensitive matters - Other Requirements:Ability to pass a background check and complete SafeSport / safeguarding training; willingness to travel and to work occasional evenings and weekends around camps and events - Language: English required - General knowledge of soccer - Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission - Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)
Desired Qualifications
- Experience within an NGB, the Olympic & Paralympic Movement, sport, or education, and with inclusive, accessible safeguarding for disabled participants and adults at risk - Spanish proficiency
U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.
U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Senior Software Engineer
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Senior Software Engineer will provide hands-on technical leadership for the shared platform capabilities that powers U.S. Soccer's Soccer Services and Learning Center experiences. This engineer will lead the design and delivery of reusable components, services, content models, and workflow patterns that can be composed across public, authenticated, learner, and administrator experiences serving coaches, referees, educators, Organization Members, players, parents, and other participants across the 

country.


Based at U.S. Soccer’s National Training Center, this role will be a visible Product & Technology partner for Soccer Services and Learning Center stakeholders. The Senior Software Engineer will participate in planning and working sessions, translate operational and product needs into clear technical direction, communicate tradeoffs and delivery risk, and build trusted relationships across engineering, product, design, content and curriculum, data, and soccer operations.


The work spans education, course management, licensing and certification, member and organization services, registration and application workflows, safeguarding and compliance, content delivery, and administrative operations. This engineer will establish and extend proven patterns across clear boundaries between experience, content, identity, and operational systems; guide incremental modernization while protecting current service; and make U.S. Soccer’s design, accessibility, security, reliability, and performance standards the default.


This is a senior individual-contributor role for a systems-oriented full-stack engineer who combines architecture judgment with a willingness to work directly in the code. Depending on the product area, the engineer may work with technologies such as Go, PHP/Laravel, JavaScript and TypeScript, Sanity, PostgreSQL, Auth0/OIDC, AWS, containers and Kubernetes, messaging platforms, and CDN/edge delivery.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical design and end-to-end delivery of production capabilities across Soccer.
  • Services and the Learning Center—from discovery and architecture through implementation, testing, release, monitoring, and iteration.
  • Serve as an in-person Product & Technology partner at the National Training Center; participate in stakeholder meetings, clarify complex requirements, surface dependencies and risks, and translate product and operational goals into practical delivery plans.
  • Establish and evolve reusable platform building blocks—including user-interface components, service contracts, content models, templates, and workflow patterns—that solve shared problems and can be adopted consistently across products.
  • Deliver learner-, member-, and administrator-facing experiences such as dashboards, course modules, video review, assessment and certification flows, renewals, progress tracking, in person clinic logistics, registration, eligibility, document review, approvals, and administrative tools.
  • Provide technical leadership through architecture and code reviews, design facilitation, documentation, mentorship, and constructive feedback; help engineers make sound decisions and raise the quality and consistency of the team’s work.
  • Design and operate backend services, APIs, data models, event-driven workflows, and integrations across identity, content, learning, member, analytics, and third-party systems, with clear contracts and strong auditability.
  • Lead incremental modernization of existing workflows and integrations while maintaining compatibility, data integrity, and reliable service for current users.
  • Set and uphold standards for automated testing, continuous delivery, observability, performance, scalability, resilience, accessibility, privacy, role-based access, and security; lead diagnosis and durable resolution of production incidents.
  • Partner with engineering and product leadership on roadmaps, technical strategy, sequencing, estimation, staffing dependencies, and measurable outcomes while communicating decisions clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in software engineering or related field. 
  • 7+ years of professional software-engineering experience building and operating production applications, including at least 3 years' operating at a senior or technical-lead level.
  • Demonstrated success leading the design and delivery of complex full-stack systems across frontend, backend, APIs, data, integrations, and cloud infrastructure.
  • Strong HTML, CSS, and modern JavaScript or TypeScript skills, plus deep experience with at least one server-side language and relational data modeling.
  • Experience designing maintainable service boundaries, web APIs, distributed or event-driven workflows, and integrations with identity or other enterprise platforms.
  • Strong understanding of software architecture, automated testing, version control, code review, continuous integration and delivery, observability, and safe production operations.
  • Experience building secure, privacy-aware, responsive, and accessible digital experiences and protecting data integrity during migrations and integrations.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose issues across application code, infrastructure, logs, metrics, and user-reported behavior; able to lead incident response and carry fixes safely into production.
  • Track record of improving engineering practices and mentoring other engineers through clear technical direction, collaborative reviews, and constructive feedback.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to build trust with nontechnical partners, facilitate decisions, and explain tradeoffs in an in-person, cross-functional environment.
  • Ability to work effectively from the National Training Center in a fast-moving environment, manage competing priorities, and connect implementation details to broader product and organizational goals.
  • General knowledge of soccer and its ecosystem, or a demonstrated interest in learning it quickly.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with technologies relevant to the current environment, such as Go, PHP/Laravel, JavaScript/TypeScript, Sanity or another headless CMS, PostgreSQL, Auth0/OIDC, or similar tools.
  • Experience designing systems with CQRS and event sourcing, and building APIs that use JSON Patch or comparable standards for partial resource updates.
  • Experience with distributed systems, asynchronous processing, and messaging or streaming platforms such as Kafka or RabbitMQ.
  • Experience deploying and operating cloud applications using AWS, containers, Kubernetes, CDN/edge services, and modern observability practices.
  • Experience building learning-management, education, certification, membership, eligibility, compliance, document-review, or other multi-role workflow products.
  • Experience with design systems, WCAG 2.1 AA, media-rich experiences, and products designed for low-bandwidth or older-device contexts.
  • Experience integrating identity, content, CRM, analytics, or third-party platforms while maintaining data quality, security, and auditability.
  • Background in or passion for soccer, sports, education, or membership-based organizations
  • Spanish-language proficiency is a plus.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

Position Description


The Software Engineer will help build and evolve the shared platform capabilities that power U.S. Soccer’s Soccer Services and Learning Center experiences. Rather than building isolated applications or one-off features, this engineer will create reusable components, services, content models, and workflow patterns that can be composed across public, authenticated, learner, and administrator experiences serving coaches, referees, educators, Organization Members, players, parents, and other participants 

across the country.


The work spans education, course management, licensing and certification, member and organization services, registration and application workflows, safeguarding and compliance, content delivery, and administrative operations. This engineer will extend proven patterns across clear boundaries between experience, content, identity, and operational systems; make U.S. Soccer’s design, accessibility, security, reliability, and performance standards the default; and modernize existing workflows incrementally 

while maintaining reliable service for current users.


The ideal candidate is a systems-oriented full-stack engineer who is comfortable moving between user facing interfaces, server-side workflows, APIs, data, integrations, and production troubleshooting. They care about making complex processes understandable, view accessibility and reliability as product requirements, and work closely with product, design, content and curriculum, operations, and subject-matter experts to build new capabilities, integrate existing systems, and operate the resulting software 

in production.


Depending on the product area, this engineer may work with technologies such as Go, PHP/Laravel, JavaScript and TypeScript, Sanity, PostgreSQL, Auth0/OIDC, AWS, containers and Kubernetes, and CDN/edge delivery. We do not expect candidates to arrive as experts in every part of the stack; strong web fundamentals, engineering judgment, and the ability to learn are more important.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Own production features end to end across Soccer Services and the Learning Center—from discovery and implementation through testing, release, monitoring, and iteration.
  • Create reusable platform building blocks—including user-interface components, service patterns, content models, templates, and workflow patterns—that solve shared problems and can be adopted across products.
  • Deliver learner- and administrator-facing experiences such as dashboards, course modules, video review, assessment and certification flows, renewals, progress tracking, in-person clinic logistics, and administrative tools; translate complex requirements involving profiles, organizations, registrations, credentials, eligibility, documents, and approvals into clear, maintainable software.
  • Develop responsive and accessible user interfaces and reusable components aligned with U.S. Soccer’s design system, building for variable connectivity, older devices, media-rich content, and a broad range of screen sizes and browsers.
  • Build and maintain backend services, APIs, data models, and integrations across identity, content, learning, member, analytics, and third-party systems, using clear contracts that support incremental modernization and compatibility with existing workflows.
  • Partner with product, design, content and curriculum, data, and operational experts across Coaching Education, Refereeing, Safeguarding, Soccer Services, and U.S. Soccer’s member ecosystem; help define requirements, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes.
  • Protect security, privacy, role-based access, auditability, and data integrity, including during migrations and integrations.
  • Improve automated testing, performance, scalability, resilience, and observability; monitor production health, diagnose incidents, and deliver durable fixes.
  • Participate in code and architecture reviews, technical planning, estimation, documentation, and disciplined release practices while communicating tradeoffs, dependencies, and delivery risk clearly.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Software Engineering or related field.
  • 3+ years of professional experience building and operating production web applications.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver features across both frontend and backend systems, including strong HTML, CSS, and modern JavaScript or TypeScript skills and experience with at least one server-side language.
  • Experience designing, consuming, and troubleshooting web APIs and working with relational databases.
  • Strong understanding of maintainable software design, automated testing, version control, code review, and continuous integration and delivery practices.
  • Experience building secure, privacy-aware, responsive, and accessible digital experiences.
  • Ability to diagnose issues across application code, integrations, infrastructure, logs, metrics, and user-reported behavior and to carry fixes safely into production.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical decisions to nontechnical partners.
  • Experience with project-management and collaboration software such as Jira and Microsoft 365.
  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment, manage competing priorities, and connect implementation details to broader product and organizational goals.
  • General knowledge of soccer and its ecosystem, or a demonstrated interest in learning it quickly.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with technologies relevant to the current environment, such as Go, PHP/Laravel, 
  • JavaScript/TypeScript, Sanity or another headless CMS, PostgreSQL, Auth0/OIDC, or similar tools.
  • Experience deploying and operating cloud applications using AWS, containers, Kubernetes, 
  • CDN/edge services, and modern observability practices.
  • Experience designing systems with CQRS and event sourcing, and building APIs that use JSON 
  • Patch or comparable standards for partial resource updates.
  • Experience building learning-management, education, certification, membership, eligibility, compliance, document-review, or other multi-role workflow products.
  • Experience with design systems, WCAG 2.1 AA, media-rich experiences, and products designed for low-bandwidth or older-device contexts.
  • Experience integrating identity, content, CRM, analytics, event-driven, or third-party platforms while maintaining data quality and auditability.
  • Background in or passion for soccer, sports, education, or membership-based organizations; 
  • Spanish-language proficiency is a plus

That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.
U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.
Position Description
The Software Engineer will help build and evolve the shared platform capabilities that power U.S. Soccer’s Soccer Services and Learning Center experiences. Rather than building isolated applications or one-off features, this engineer will create reusable components, services, content models, and workflow patterns that can be composed across public, authenticated, learner, and administrator experiences serving coaches, referees, educators, Organization Members, players, parents, and other participants
across the country.
The work spans education, course management, licensing and certification, member and organization services, registration and application workflows, safeguarding and compliance, content delivery, and administrative operations. This engineer will extend proven patterns across clear boundaries between experience, content, identity, and operational systems; make U.S. Soccer’s design, accessibility, security, reliability, and performance standards the default; and modernize existing workflows incrementally
while maintaining reliable service for current users.
The ideal candidate is a systems-oriented full-stack engineer who is comfortable moving between user facing interfaces, server-side workflows, APIs, data, integrations, and production troubleshooting. They care about making complex processes understandable, view accessibility and reliability as product requirements, and work closely with product, design, content and curriculum, operations, and subject-matter experts to build new capabilities, integrate existing systems, and operate the resulting software
in production.
Depending on the product area, this engineer may work with technologies such as Go, PHP/Laravel, JavaScript and TypeScript, Sanity, PostgreSQL, Auth0/OIDC, AWS, containers and Kubernetes, and CDN/edge delivery. We do not expect candidates to arrive as experts in every part of the stack; strong web fundamentals, engineering judgment, and the ability to learn are more important.
Primary Responsibilities
- Own production features end to end across Soccer Services and the Learning Center—from discovery and implementation through testing, release, monitoring, and iteration. - Create reusable platform building blocks—including user-interface components, service patterns, content models, templates, and workflow patterns—that solve shared problems and can be adopted across products. - Deliver learner- and administrator-facing experiences such as dashboards, course modules, video review, assessment and certification flows, renewals, progress tracking, in-person clinic logistics, and administrative tools; translate complex requirements involving profiles, organizations, registrations, credentials, eligibility, documents, and approvals into clear, maintainable software. - Develop responsive and accessible user interfaces and reusable components aligned with U.S. Soccer’s design system, building for variable connectivity, older devices, media-rich content, and a broad range of screen sizes and browsers. - Build and maintain backend services, APIs, data models, and integrations across identity, content, learning, member, analytics, and third-party systems, using clear contracts that support incremental modernization and compatibility with existing workflows. - Partner with product, design, content and curriculum, data, and operational experts across Coaching Education, Refereeing, Safeguarding, Soccer Services, and U.S. Soccer’s member ecosystem; help define requirements, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes. - Protect security, privacy, role-based access, auditability, and data integrity, including during migrations and integrations. - Improve automated testing, performance, scalability, resilience, and observability; monitor production health, diagnose incidents, and deliver durable fixes. - Participate in code and architecture reviews, technical planning, estimation, documentation, and disciplined release practices while communicating tradeoffs, dependencies, and delivery risk clearly.
Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor's Degree in Software Engineering or related field. - 3+ years of professional experience building and operating production web applications. - Demonstrated ability to deliver features across both frontend and backend systems, including strong HTML, CSS, and modern JavaScript or TypeScript skills and experience with at least one server-side language. - Experience designing, consuming, and troubleshooting web APIs and working with relational databases. - Strong understanding of maintainable software design, automated testing, version control, code review, and continuous integration and delivery practices. - Experience building secure, privacy-aware, responsive, and accessible digital experiences. - Ability to diagnose issues across application code, integrations, infrastructure, logs, metrics, and user-reported behavior and to carry fixes safely into production. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical decisions to nontechnical partners. - Experience with project-management and collaboration software such as Jira and Microsoft 365. - Ability to work effectively in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment, manage competing priorities, and connect implementation details to broader product and organizational goals. - General knowledge of soccer and its ecosystem, or a demonstrated interest in learning it quickly. - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission. - Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
Desired Qualifications
- Experience with technologies relevant to the current environment, such as Go, PHP/Laravel, - JavaScript/TypeScript, Sanity or another headless CMS, PostgreSQL, Auth0/OIDC, or similar tools. - Experience deploying and operating cloud applications using AWS, containers, Kubernetes, - CDN/edge services, and modern observability practices. - Experience designing systems with CQRS and event sourcing, and building APIs that use JSON - Patch or comparable standards for partial resource updates. - Experience building learning-management, education, certification, membership, eligibility, compliance, document-review, or other multi-role workflow products. - Experience with design systems, WCAG 2.1 AA, media-rich experiences, and products designed for low-bandwidth or older-device contexts. - Experience integrating identity, content, CRM, analytics, event-driven, or third-party platforms while maintaining data quality and auditability. - Background in or passion for soccer, sports, education, or membership-based organizations; - Spanish-language proficiency is a plus
U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.
U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Photographer, Men's National Team
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is seeking an experienced photographer to join our Men’s National Team content team as the team photographer. The MNT Photographer will be responsible for capturing and telling the story of our MNT players and staff through compelling imagery, highlighting The Best of U.S™.


This role leads still photography coverage for the MNT across all environments, including camps, matches, training sessions, and behind-the-scenes moments. The position owns the end-to-end photography process: shooting, editing, color grading, selecting, and delivering imagery optimized for real-time distribution and licensing across platforms.


There is a strong emphasis on speed to market, especially during camps and matchdays, ensuring content is delivered in real time to support social, editorial, and commercial objectives.


This individual will collaborate closely with Social Media, Brand and Creative, Media, Editorial, Content Strategy, and Partnership Marketing to ensure photography supports storytelling, audience growth, and revenue-driving initiatives including photo licensing, Insiders, ticket sales, and partner integrations.


While this role is dedicated to the MNT, it operates as part of a centralized content function and will support broader Federation photography needs during key moments and priority initiatives.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Capture high-quality photography of USMNT camps, matches, training sessions, and off-field moments
  • Deliver real-time and near real-time photo selects for distribution across social and owned platforms
  • Edit, color correct, and optimize imagery for various formats, platforms, and audiences
  • Curate and deliver photo selects for U.S. Soccer’s photo licensing and sales partner
  • Collaborate with Social Media and Editorial teams to align on storytelling priorities and platform needs
  • Execute content plans around camps and matches, ensuring full coverage of key moments and narratives
  • Maintain and organize photo assets within U.S. Soccer’s digital asset management system
  • Conceptualize and contribute to new content series and storytelling approaches in collaboration with Content Strategy
  • Support commercial initiatives through photography, including photo licensing, partner content, Insiders growth, and ticket sales
  • Stay current with industry trends, technology, and best practices in sports and editorial photography
  • Travel extensively with the team, including domestic and international travel
  • Cover other Federation events, camps and games as needed.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years of professional photography experience, preferably in sports or live event environments
  • Proven ability to capture high-quality imagery in fast-paced, high-pressure environments
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating storytelling through photography
  • Expertise in DSLR/mirrorless camera systems and professional lenses
  • Proficiency in Photo Mechanic (or equivalent), Adobe Lightroom, and Adobe Photoshop
  • Familiarity with digital asset management systems
  • Strong understanding of photo composition, lighting, and color grading
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects under tight deadlines
  • General knowledge of soccer
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)
  • Ability to work non-traditional hours including nights, weekends, and holidays
  • Willingness to travel up to 50% domestically and internationally
  • Valid passport required


Desired Qualifications

  • Experience working with elite athletes or professional sports teams
  • Understanding of content optimization across social and digital platforms
  • Knowledge of soccer and its global landscape
  • Experience capturing stylized, lifestyle photography



U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is seeking a Coordinator, Content Operations to support the operational workflows and systems that power the Federation’s growing content ecosystem.


This role will support content production, project coordination, media asset management and production logistics across video, photography and post-production teams. They will help manage day-to-day workflows, maintain project organization and assist in ensuring content initiatives move efficiently from intake through delivery and archival.


The Coordinator, Content Operations will also support the organization and management of the Federation’s media libraries across platforms including Iconik and PhotoShelter, helping ensure assets are properly archived, tagged and accessible for future use.


The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented and eager to grow within a fast-paced content and production environment. This individual should be comfortable managing multiple projects simultaneously, collaborating across departments and helping support operational processes that enable efficient, high-quality content production across the Federation.


Primary Responsibilities

    

Content Operations & Project Management

  • Support the day-to-day management of the department’s content intake and project tracking workflows
  • Assist in coordinating timelines, deliverables and project communication across content initiatives Help maintain project trackers, production schedules and operational calendars
  •  Coordinate with internal stakeholders across video, social media, editorial, photography and strategy teams to support content execution
  • Help ensure projects are properly organized, scoped and operationalized throughout the production lifecycle
  • Assist in identifying workflow bottlenecks and operational inefficiencies, escalating issues as needed
  • Support departmental organization and operational documentation, including templates, workflows and process tracking

Media Asset Management (MAM/DAM)

  • Support the day-to-day organization and maintenance of media asset management systems, including Iconik and PhotoShelter
  • Assist with media ingest, tagging, metadata entry and archival workflows across photo and video assets
  • Help maintain consistent file naming conventions, folder structures and metadata standards
  • Support asset retrieval requests and content distribution workflows for internal stakeholders
  • Assist in maintaining organized, searchable and accessible media libraries across Federation content

Production Logistics & Photography Operations 

  • Assist with production logistics, including vendor coordination, scheduling support, releases, clearances and production preparation
  • Help coordinate photography assignments, shot lists and coverage schedules
  • Support equipment coordination, file delivery and production organization as needed
  • Assist with freelancer and vendor communication for content productions
  • Support operational workflows tied to content delivery and asset distribution

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience in content operations, production coordination, media management or related fields
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Experience managing multiple projects and deadlines in fast-paced environments
  • Familiarity with Digital Asset Management (DAM) and/or Media Asset Management (MAM) systems such as Iconik, PhotoShelter or similar platforms
  • Understanding of content production workflows across video, photography and digital media
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills
  • General knowledge of soccer
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace and project management tool
  • Ability to work independently while supporting multiple stakeholders and priorities
  • Must be able to connect "micro" details to the "macro" vision and mission
  • Willingness to work non-traditional hours and travel as needed

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience working within sports, media, entertainment or agency environments
  • Familiarity with video production, photography or post-production workflows
  • Experience supporting project management or production operations
  • Understanding of metadata organization and archival best practices
  • Experience coordinating production logistics or photography operations
  • Spanish language proficiency is a plus
  • Understanding of U.S. Soccer and its content ecosystem


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Player Scout Manager – Women’s College
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

  

Reporting into the WNT Assistant Coach & Player Scout Manager and in collaboration with our Women’s Talent ID management team, the Women’s College Player Scout Manager is responsible for overseeing scouting, tracking, and monitoring of high potentials across NCAA landscape. The role involves leading all aspects of U.S. Soccer’s Women’s College Talent ID Plan and developing intimate knowledge and relationships with key NCAA programs and members to gather detailed information and drive an accurate, efficient, evidence based, and collaborative decision-making and player selection process.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Commits to the mission, objectives, values, and policies of U.S. Soccer and The U.S. Way (and her LENS)
  • Applies U.S. Soccer Talent Identification Strategy, Philosophy, Framework, Processes and Structures 
  • Creates, drives, executes, and evolves a unified strategic scouting plan for women’s college landscape
  • Collaborates with Talent ID department, Women’s National Team Coaches, Integrated Sports Performance, National Team Player Scouts, YNT Scouting Network, and Talent Reporters
  • Identifies, tracks, monitors, and recommends players to expand and improve player pools U-17 through U-23.
  • Expands and improves the College Scouting Network
  • Serves as Player Scout Lead for specific YNT age group, as assigned by Player Scout Manager, Senior Managers, and Head of Talent ID
  • Manages online technology platforms for reporting, tracking, and longitudinal monitoring—applies data and creates video clips to produce player profiles
  • Contributes to US Way and herLENS technical Projects, as assigned
  • Communicates effectively with all internal and external stakeholders (players, staff, scouts, colleges, coaches, etc.)
  • Completes a personal development plan and reviews with direct report on an annual basis

  

Role and tasks of the position are based on 3 Key Areas: College Scouting, Building and Managing YNT Scouting Network, and Technology & Analysis

  

College Scouting 

  • Strategically and systematically manages player identification, tracking and weekly scouting assignments (video and in-person) for key games, training sessions, tournaments across NCAA Division 1
  • Maintains college depth charts (long lists, short lists) and collaborates with TIDM age group lead on age group depth charts
  • Creates, submits, presents, and reviews player reports using WNT templates (written and video, attention to details)
  • Cross-checks reports and recommends players for YNT camps as part of longitudinal and collaborative selection and decision-making process
  • Attends key days at YNT age group camps to support assessment process and gain knowledge of current player pool when making comparisons and recommendations. As assigned and approved by Player Scout Manager
  • Attends/Co-Leads weekly TID/College Age Group Teams Meetings to review players
  • Serve in lead role for a YNT age group as assigned by Player Scout Manager
  • Attends key NCAA games and events in-person (i.e. Women’s College Cup, NWSL Combines, etc.)

Building and Managing YNT Scouting Network 

  • Builds, manages, and develops a quality, diverse and reliable network of independent/part-time Scouts across the NCAA landscape (follows all protocols for vetting, recruiting, hiring, and onboarding new scouts in areas of need)
  • Assigns scouts to weekly games, training sessions and annual events based on TID strategy and plan
  • Reviews all scout reports for quality control. Provides feedback, supports development, and organizes a mentoring system for YNT Network Scouts
  • Builds a supplementary network with members, colleges, Talent Reporters, and tipsters (informal leads) 
  • Supports scouting initiatives for Behind the Badge, under-served communities and outreach programs

Technology & Analysis (Player Monitoring Systems) 

  • Monitors players continuously over time (reports, documents, logbooks, etc.)
  • Creates video clips to support player examination and reviews
  • Applies data and statistics for quantitative analysis of player
  • Supports development of internal W-NCAA data dashboards and systems to support scouting 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
  • U.S. Soccer Talent Scout License or equivalent (required to successfully complete year 1 if does not currently hold license)
  • High level ability to lead, plan, and collaborate
  • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to develop and maintain relationships
  • Passion for scouting and experience within a college and/or high-performance environment
  • Possesses a growth mindset
  • Comprehensive knowledge of the NCAA landscape/pathway 
  • Competencies, characteristics and understanding of talent identification and development—process, structure, theory, and practice (international and domestic standards) 
  • Soccer experience and game understanding that contribute to assessing and interpreting player actions and behaviors to produce clear player profiles (Potential and Performance)
  • Proficient with analysis, reporting, video clipping, data, and scout technology platforms (Sportscode, Wyscout, Hudl, Statsbomb, etc)
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook)
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Excellent verbal and written communication combined with a professional demeanor 
  • Able and willing to work/travel throughout the year, with an understanding that in-person assignments will be balanced with video scouting
  • Able and willing to work non-traditional hours including evenings, weekends and holidays as needed

Other

  • Participate in U.S. Soccer Talent Scout Courses and herLENS workshops for ongoing education and development, as assigned by Player Scout Manager and Head of Talent ID


Desired Qualifications

  • Professional playing experience
  • Bilingual (English and Spanish)


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.plain_text_description:
Football Development Coach (Casual)
This is an exciting opportunity to deliver on our Football Development activities at one or more of our locations: Wolverhampton, Telford, Shrewsbury, Codsall, Newport, Cannock or Stafford and to support the international programme.
This role involves coaching across the Football Development programme and working with other staff to deliver high-quality sessions updating player tracking and liaising with full-time staff on the evaluation of players.
Please note that this is a casual role.
For more details on this role and the requirements, please see the job description.
Ref - JH-025-23082024

General Steward (Casual)

Stewards are deployed to assist in the safe operation of Molineux Stadium before, during and after events.

For more details on this role and the requirements, please see the job description.

If you'd like to be considered for this role please complete the General Steward Application Form and Diversity Monitoring Form (links located on the job description) and email to stadium@wolves.co.uk

job.title: Host Families Required
job.html_description:
Host Families Required

Wolves are seeking host families who can provide accommodation for Academy players aged 14-19 years. Our ideal Host family provision will be able to offer our young players a stable, safe and comfortable environment. We believe our players perform better on the pitch when they are settled and content at home.

At Wolves we pride ourselves on a nurturing environment and we want our players to fulfil their potential both ON and OFF the pitch.

For more details on how to register your interest in becoming a host family, please see the Host Families Description below.

All queries and applications should be directed to hostfamily@wolves.co.uk

job.title: Turnstile Operator (Casual)
job.html_description:
Turnstile Operator (Casual)

To admit spectators, check tickets.

Turnstile operators are not expected to be involved with searching or ejecting spectators or dealing with conflict. Their role is specific, and they will be expected to call on a supervisor or specialist stewards for assistance in dealing with any incident at their turnstile.

Turnstile Operators are supported by search stewards and a supervisor. 

For more details on this role and the requirements, please see the below job description.

Ref: AR-296-06072022

job.html_description:
Women & Girls Assistant Strength & Conditioning Development Coach

Following our recent promotion to the WSL2, We have an exciting opportunity to join us here at Wolves as a Women & Girls Assistant Strength & Conditioning Development Coach.

The successful candidate will look to support the Physical Development services & help support a clear and progressive pathway, whilst also offering support to medical and performance staff within the 1st Team.

job.html_description:
Women's & Girls Day Release/First Team Coach

Another great opportunity has arisen to work within our Women and Girls department as a Women's & Girls Day Release/First Team Coach.

The successful candidate will support the Women's and Girls Football programme here at Wolves by leading the delivery of the Day release programme whilst providing high quality coaching support to the Women's first team on designated training & matchdays, working closely with the Women's Head Coach & Wider MDT.

For more details on the role and its requirements, Please see the below job description.
